I farm the same 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 12 mu into wheat in the winter season and all 12 mu into maize after wheat harvest in the summer season. I do not like making big changes at my age. I start from what I did before and what I see nearby people doing. If fertilizer looks a little heavy, I can still bear that cost, but if I cut too much and the yield falls, that hurts more. Wheat needs steady fertilizer and two or three waters from my well if the weather is dry. Maize grows fast after the rains come, but I still keep water ready and feed it enough urea-type fertilizer, because if maize stays pale, yield drops fast. I will use improved seed if I can get the same kind people around here have been using well. I will keep tillage simple with rotary work, spray a couple of times for weeds and bugs, and aim for a solid harvest instead of taking chances.
